security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU TCG, when menvcfg.MT_ASYNC is set and a tag-mismatching regular store executes, the software check exception must be deferred to the next trap. If QEMU stores the pending mismatch flag and the faulting virtual address (destined for stval2/htval2/mtval3) in a non-per-CPU location, or fails to clear them on writes to menvcfg/mseccfg that disable tagging, or fails to flush them on privilege-mode transitions, then (a) one hart's trap handler can observe another hart's faulting virtual address in these CSRs, or (b) a guest can read stale virtual addresses from a prior security context after toggling MT_ASYNC off and back on.
security_spec.summary: Deferred async MTE tag mismatch state in TCG risks cross-CPU info leak via stval2/htval2/mtval3 if pending buffer is not per-hart and not sanitized on mode transitions

findings.finding: MENVCFG has no MT_ASYNC or MTE-related field. MENVCFG_PBMTE is Page-Based Memory Types (Svpbmt), not Memory Tagging Extension. The vulnerability condition's menvcfg.MT_ASYNC bit does not exist in this RISC-V implementation.

MSECCFG CSR fields (MML, MMWP, RLB, USEED, SSEED, MLPE, PMM) are exclusively for ePMP/Zkr/MLPE/power management — no MTE tag-enable bits exist. Writing menvcfg/mseccfg cannot toggle any tagging feature because none exists.
findings.snippet:
MSECCFG_MML   = 1 << 0,
MSECCFG_MMWP  = 1 << 1,
MSECCFG_RLB   = 1 << 2,
MSECCFG_USEED = 1 << 8,
MSECCFG_SSEED = 1 << 9,
MSECCFG_MLPE =  1 << 10,
MSECCFG_PMM = 3ULL << 32,

findings.finding: No stval2, htval2, or mtval3 CSR registrations exist in the CSR dispatch table. These CSRs — the destinations for the faulting virtual address described in the vulnerability — are not implemented in the RISC-V target.

riscv_cpu_do_interrupt() contains no MTE-related logic — no pending-tag-mismatch flag is checked, propagated, or flushed. No deferred async trap is injected. The vulnerability's entire mechanism (deferring tag-mismatch to next trap, loading stval2/mtval3 with faulting VA) has no code path.

CPURISCVState has no pending-tag-mismatch flag, no faulting VA storage for async tag checks, no mte_active field, and no per-CPU tag state buffer. The entire vulnerability surface — non-per-CPU location for pending mismatch — does not exist because no such state exists.
No stval2/htval2/mtval3 fields in vmstate_riscv_cpu. Migration correctness is not at risk because none of the relevant MTE async state exists to migrate.
The only modified file in this branch adds an IOMMU validation check (rejecting BARE GATP with non-OFF MSIPTP mode). This is unrelated to MTE, memory tagging, or the vulnerability described.
